thread:
anya: Quick sync — proposing a small IA shift for the left rail to reduce cognitive load for users who jump between Models and Workloads. Draft mock in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (preview)

mike: skimmed — looks promising. What's the main change vs current grouping?

anya: current: Projects / Models / Workloads / Settings. Proposal: Workspace (workspace-level items), Deployments (Workloads + Routes), Models (model catalog + versions), Observability, Settings. Trying to group by intent: manage vs run vs observe.

jamal: for routing we need to be careful. Deep links must keep a stable URL contract or we'll break bookmarks. Do we have route examples?

anya: yes — rough sketch of routes:

```js
/app/:workspaceId/overview
/app/:workspaceId/deployments/:deploymentId
/app/:workspaceId/models/:modelId
/app/:workspaceId/models/:modelId/versions/:versionId
/app/:workspaceId/observability/traces/:traceId
```

olivia: PM + UX question: when you click a deep link to a model version, should the left rail auto-expand to Models > modelName and set a visible breadcrumb? Important for discoverability.

sam: I think yes, but we have two UX problems: (1) focus & keyboard a11y when you land directly on a nested route; (2) what is the canonical URL for a model page vs model version page — we need canonicalization to de-dupe in analytics.

ada-a11y: ada-a11y here — landing focus is critical. If a user opens a deep link, we should programmatically set focus to the main page H1 and provide a skip link to the left rail. Expanding the rail is fine but don’t auto-move keyboard focus into the rail. Also breadcrumb markup should use nav[aria-label] and ol[aria-hidden=false] semantics.

mike: engineering note: current router is path-based with optional query params for filters. If we add auto-expand behavior we'll need to expose a small client-side map that maps path -> nav section id. Something like:

```json
{
  "/models": "nav-models",
  "/models/:modelId": "nav-models",
  "/deployments": "nav-deployments",
  "/deployments/:id": "nav-deployments"
}
```

That map lives in the nav component and also in server-rendered metadata for quick lookup.

jamal: +1. Also suggest that we preserve query params when following deep links (e.g., ?variant=quantized) — that should be part of the deep link contract.

olivia: one more: breadcrumbs copy. Current breadcrumb shows Workspace > {page}. Can we do: Workspace name (linked) > Area (e.g., Models) > Resource name? So model version becomes: Acme Workspace > Models > T-Rex v1.2

anya: yes. Also proposing a tiny affordance: a chevron on the left rail group header which on hover shows a permalinks menu for the group — quick copy link to Models list, or to the last-opened model. Handy for sharing in Slack.

ada-a11y: permalinks menu is okay but remember to make it keyboard reachable and label it properly (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded states). And announcements for screen readers when the menu opens.

sam: curious about analytics: if we make group headers canonical landing points, we should standardize events: nav.group_click, nav.deep_link_open, page.load_source = "deep_link|nav|internal"

mike: implementation challenge: we have server-side redirects for legacy URLs (/workspace/:id/model?id=123). Need a small router shim to canonicalize legacy -> new paths so we don't lose SEO/bookmarks. I'll add a redirect table.

anya: design nit — should breadcrumb names be truncated? Long model names (200 chars) blow the layout. Proposal: show full name in tooltip, limit visible crumb to ~40 chars with ellipsis.

olivia: good call. Add copy tweak: breadcrumb separators should be small chevrons, and use contextual aria-labels like "breadcrumb: Models > T-Rex v1.2" for screen readers.

jamal: what about URL params for state (e.g., sidepanel open=true). We should avoid encoding ephemeral UI state in the canonical URL. Use ephemeral params only for shareable state (filters, variant selection), not transient UI toggles.

design-bot: Reminder: follow-up required. Please add "nav route map" doc to the design folder and tag eng + a11y reviewers. (reaction: :bell:)

mike: timeline: I can spike the router shim and nav map in the next sprint (ETA: 2 weeks). Will warn if redirects are messy.

anya: action items — I'll update the Figma and upload final IA tiles; olivia will confirm copy for crumb labels and link language; sam to write analytics spec; mike to prototype router shim; ada-a11y to sign off on focus/aria behavior.

olivia: sounds good — i'll create tickets and link them here once ready. :thumbsup:

sam: thumbs up. Minor ask: add a short QA checklist for deep link regression (bookmark test, query param preservation, screen reader landing test).

anya: added to notes. Thanks all!"
